topicName: Artifact Management and Package Registries (Nexus, Artifactory, Container Registries)
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Artifact Management and Package Registries in CI/CD"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Artifact management is a critical component of modern Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipelines. It involves storing, versioning, and securing build outputs (such as JARs, npm packages, Docker images, and NuGet packages) so they can be reliably consumed across environments."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Why Artifact Management Matters"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Immutability: Ensures that once an artifact is built and published, its content never changes."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Dependency Caching: Speeds up CI/CD builds by downloading external dependencies from a local proxy rather than the public internet."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Traceability: Links binaries directly back to the exact Git commit and CI/CD build run that generated them."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Popular Artifact Management Solutions"},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"JFrog Artifactory: A universal artifact repository supporting dozens of package formats with robust replication and security features."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Sonatype Nexus: An enterprise-grade repository manager widely used for Java, JavaScript, and container artifacts."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Container Registries: Specialized registries like Docker Hub, AWS ECR, Google Artifact Registry, and Harbor designed for OCI-compliant container images."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuring a CI/CD Pipeline to Publish Artifacts"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is an example of a GitHub Actions workflow snippet that authenticates with a package registry and publishes a build artifact."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"name: Publish Artifact\\non:\\n  release:\\n    types: [published]\\njobs:\\n  publish:\\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\\n    steps:\\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v3\\n      - name: Set up Node.js\\n        uses: actions/setup-node@v3\\n        with:\\n          node-version: '18'\\n          registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org/'\\n      - name: Install dependencies and build\\n        run: npm ci && npm run build\\n      - name: Publish package\\n        run: npm publish\\n        env:\\n          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Registry Management"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use virtual repositories to combine local releases, snapshots, and remote proxies into a single URL for developers and CI pipelines."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Implement automated retention and cleanup policies to delete old snapshot builds and free up storage."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Integrate vulnerability scanning (Xray, Trivy) directly into the registry to block deployment of vulnerable packages."}]
